summary: For each successful call of estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2, write the pallet width, height, and depth in metres on the stage-2 outcome and on PalletPoseStamped after deferred_source_indices. Width is params.pallet_width_m and height is params.pallet_height_m, the factory face cached_prototype already passes to build_default_pallet_prototype, and the search template stays that face. The face-centre position and yaw stay the pose, and pose.position.z stays centre_r.z(), the range lift_point_from_plane_2d and apply_se3 already store for the face centre. The admitted source index and the deferred source indices stay the lists published_admission_split already writes. The two fork openings are the pocket centres build_default_pallet_prototype already cuts, at (-pocket_centre_offset_m, 0) and (+pocket_centre_offset_m, 0) in prototype coordinates, with the pocket sides that call already uses. Place those two points with transform_points_2d at best_pose, lift each with lift_point_from_plane_2d on the same plane basis as the face centre, and map each into the camera RGB optical frame with apply_se3 of camera_cfg.R_dr and camera_cfg.t_dr. Write those two centres on the outcome and, after depth_m, on PalletPoseStamped, the negative-offset centre first. Depth is the mean of those two centres' z in that RGB frame, the optical depth of the openings this match placed. It is not a median or a slab of sample_face_points, not the inlier span, and not padding_m. On a frontal face the two centres share the face centre's optical depth; on a tilted face they do not, and pose.position.z remains the face centre. This pass does not draw from the node rng. It runs before return, while best_pose and the plane basis are still locals, and publish_pose copies the three sizes and the two centres. A failed estimate still publishes no PalletPoseStamped, and the failure diagnostic stays the admission lists it already carries. The two early returns in on_pair stay silent. Stage 2 still runs once, on the one candidate the admission split already admits. The rich message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the sizes and the openings belong to this capture while the scene can still change. The user named the three sizes. The part they did not name is that depth is the optical depth of the two fork openings this match already cuts, and that those two centres are on the pose result the handling process reads.
hypothesis: PalletPoseStamped already carries this capture's face centre, yaw, and admission split, while the fork openings stay inside the prototype the match already uses. Lifting those two centres into the RGB frame, and writing the factory face with their optical depth onto the pose result, gives the handling process the width, height, and depth of the pallet it is about to approach at the openings the forks enter.
